description: Somos ONE MISSION X, un equipo de 4 estudiantes con diferentes habilidades, unidos por una misma misión: aprender, crear y convertir ideas en soluciones. Nos interesan la tecnología, programación, ciencia, datos, diseño y comunicación. Estamos abiertos a sumar hasta 2 integrantes con curiosidad, creatividad, compromiso y ganas de aprender. No buscamos expertos, sino personas dispuestas a aportar y trabajar en equipo.
summary: Earth Information Jukebox transforms active natural events from NASA EONET into interactive records that combine data, satellite imagery, and sound. The application displays up to ten open events and retrieves NASA GIBS imagery for each event’s location, date, and category. When the user presses Play, the app sorts geolocated observations chronologically and generates notes in real time: magnitude affects intensity and duration, latitude helps determine pitch, and longitude controls stereo position. Timbre and variation are calculated using a consistent signature for each event and repeatable variation for each note. The project aims to make changes on our planet more explorable and accessible by letting people hear the data they see. The current version uses EONET and GIBS; direct integration with Earth Information Center visualizations could be a future step.
details:
The creative idea is to turn each natural event into a record in a jukebox. The shelf groups active events by category, and the player displays event details alongside related satellite imagery. The application retrieves up to ten open events from NASA EONET, including available dates, locations, and magnitudes. NASA GIBS provides imagery selected according to each event’s area, date, and related image layers.

When the user presses Play, geolocated observations are sorted by date and converted into notes using the Web Audio API. Magnitude affects intensity and duration; latitude helps determine the notes; and longitude moves the sound from left to right. The event’s category and identity help determine its timbre, while repeatable variations change some details between notes. The visualizer shows the generated audio signal, rather than a direct graph of the measurements.

The project uses HTML, CSS, PHP, and vanilla JavaScript. It includes PWA features such as installation, resource caching, and access to the most recently saved EONET data when a connection is unavailable. Live GIBS imagery requires an internet connection. The interface also supports keyboard navigation and reduced-motion preferences.

AI use disclosure: Generative AI assistants, including Claude and ChatGPT, were used to help write and translate text, and to generate, review, and debug parts of the code. Event data and satellite imagery come from NASA EONET and NASA GIBS. Audio is synthesized through programmed rules using the Web Audio API; it is not AI-generated.
